## Responsibility

MetatorAI Desktop (D7, ADR-0078): the Vite + React app and its Tauri shell, a thin client over `metator serve`. It draws the chats (threads, round 16: one topic each, with its chat terminal as the main view, `#/thread/<id>`) and three levels: the tasks (the sidebar, Home with one decision at a time, the Board), a task's page (Overview with its decision, flow and steps · Changes · Activity) and a step's page (Overview with its plan · Terminal over the daemon's PTY · Changes · Activity); then Terminals (every terminal at once, filtered and grouped; a task's main terminal and its repository sessions; a session's sub-terminals), the backlog, Reviews (watched MRs and my MRs, round 18), Settings (options, System) and the new-run form; it decides nothing and keeps no state the daemon does not have.

## Invariants

- The app carries no code of MetatorAI. From `@metator/core` it takes types only, with a whole-statement `import type` (ADR-0085, MT-ARCH-010); the shapes the daemon composes itself are typed in the client [[cite: packages/desktop/src/shared/api/api.ts:2 | "The daemon's JSON and WebSockets, as the app sees them"]].
- An answer from the decision card carries `origin: inbox`, what criterion 11a counts [[cite: packages/desktop/src/features/inbox/decision-card.tsx:121 | "origin: \"inbox\","]].
- Layers point one way (ADR-0109, MT-ARCH-011..013): `app/` (the shell) → `features/<name>/` (a screen and its parts) → `shared/` (api, daemon state, platform, view model) → `ui/` (the design system). View logic is pure in `model.ts` files (`shared/model/`, a feature's own) and tested; components only render. The daemon's state is a store read by field (`useDaemon(...fields)`), and a polled request is a query whose equal answer keeps the last one's objects (ADR-0108): an idle app draws nothing.
- One vocabulary for states: what a pane reads as is `paneStateOf` (`working`, `asks`, `idle`, `exited`), and the glyph and colour of every state come from `LOOKS` through `<Glyph>`; a screen never has its own table. A shell is never `asks` and is `working` only while it prints.
- One count and one roll-up: what needs the person is `needsQueue` (the sidebar counts it, Home shows it one at a time with next/previous, one address per decision, `decisionKey`, and per pane question of a pane without a run, `paneAskKey`, shown by `PaneAskCard` and answered with `answerPane`); a run's fine word is `runStateOf`, rolled up pane → run through `rollUp`; the first level (sidebar, Home, Board, page heads) says only `firstLevel`'s five words (`needs you`, `working`, `blocked`, `to do` for a backlog task not started, `done`) with `LOOKS.first`, a blocked thing's reason is `blockedReason`. `done` is a finished run this person has not opened; what was opened is kept in the window's storage (`metator.seen`), read and written under try/catch.
- One row pattern in the sidebar: glyph, name, the state's word, one dim line (`runLine`, `taskLine`, `threadLine`); no ids, hosts, ages or chips on the first level (they are in a step's Details), no counters in the top bar (its scope counts repositories, `folderLabel`: a worktree is a place, `Place.worktreeOf`, named `shop (fix-tax)` by `placeLabel` in the pickers, with `· N worktrees` beside them); finished tasks hide behind "Show finished (N)" in each group. The sidebar is one hierarchy, thread → its tasks → repositories → steps (`threadTree` in `src/shared/model/threads.ts`, pure): a task is a thread's when the thread's `runs` hold its top run (in a folder, in the thread's repository); the rest is "Without a chat" (derived, shown only when non-empty); closed threads are under "Closed (N)", folded, with their tasks. A thread row's word is `threadWord`: `needs you` when its chat asks, else its most urgent open task's (needs you, blocked, working, done), `done` when all are finished, `chat` (its own look, `LOOKS.chat`) with none. Threads: needs you first, then the newest change of the thread or its tasks. The threads come from `GET /threads` (open and closed), read again when `/state`'s `threads` stamp changes (`threadsStamp`). "+ New chat" (and `n`, and Home's "Describe a task", titled `chatTitleOf`) is `POST /threads` with the first installed host; a thread created from the one on screen (`from.thread`, the agent's topic change) is followed once (`followedThread`). Close and Reopen are `POST /threads/:id/close|reopen`; closing never stops a run. Home's tasks carry their thread's title as a dim prefix (`threadTitleOf`).
- One page per run: `#/run/<run>/<tab>`, a task's or a step's (`runPage` in `tasks.ts`, tabs from `tabsOf`); old routes (the Plan tab, `#/overview`, `#/mrs`, `#/settings/reviews`) parse to the place that holds what they showed.
- One word per thing: a unit of work is a run, a session is the live agent process, a task is a backlog item, the multi-pane place is Terminals, the diff is Changes. One letter, one meaning: the single-letter keys of `SHELL_KEYS` are listed once each and the tabs of a run use theirs (a test checks it).
- Shared pieces are written once: a request on an interval is `usePolled` (a TanStack Query query, `src/shared/api/query.ts`), read again when the daemon's `/ws/events` names its topic (`topicOfKey`, `readEvent` in `src/shared/api/events.ts`; for the topics the daemon sweeps, `SWEPT`, polling is then a fallback, ADR-0110); a screen opens a run with `useOpenRun`, says a notice with `say` (`shared/notice.ts`) and opens the help or the form through `shared/overlays.ts`, never through callbacks from the shell; an action with its refusal that stays is `useAction`; attach, release, the editor and "Open a session" of a run are `runControls`; one option is `useOption` (the options are read once, in `DaemonProvider`); an answer to a question is `useAnswer`; a single-letter shortcut is `plainKey`; the person's name is `who()` (one dialog). Shared markup is written once: a list screen is `<ListDetail>` with `<ListRow>` (the arrow keys and `j`/`k` move in it, `moveInList`); the top of a run's page is `<RunHeader>` (breadcrumb, name, word, progress, tabs, Details); the stages are `<StageBar>`; events are `<ActivityList>`; a row of tabs is `<Tabs>`; a dialog is `<Modal>` (the browser's `<dialog>`).
- The workbench's commands are named once in `WORKBENCH_COMMANDS` (`src/shared/model/keys.ts`): the keys, both right-click menus and the help overlay read that table. Terminals is by task: the tree (main terminal, a session per child run, its sub-terminals) is `terminalTasks` in `terminals.ts` (pure); an ended pane stays read-only with `endedBanner` until a person closes it, drawing its last screen (`lastScreen`: a full-screen program such as Claude Code leaves the alternate screen as it exits, so the stream is cut where it left it); a paused one (`pausedOf`) is not ended and continues (`toContinue`, Continue task). With no task chosen Terminals shows every terminal (`#/grid/all`, round 22): rows with repository, role, state and parent (`terminalRows`), groups (`groupRows`), the filter (`passes`, `toggleFilter`: Alt+click only this, again all; `showing` opens it just enough for a link), a repository's mark (`repoMark`: the same two letters and hue everywhere; the folder's repositories take distinct hues in sorted order), all pure in `terminals.ts`; the filter and the grouping are the window's (`metator.terminals`, `terminalViewFromStorage`).
- Plans are never edited in the app (ADR-0089): a plan's approval card shows it in full and "Ask for changes" answers the gate's Reject with the person's words. The document editor (`features/plans/doc-editor.tsx`) is the system map's only: a document view from the daemon, a draft as fields or as JSON text, **Check** = the daemon's lint without saving, **Save…** = what changes (`features/plans/plan-edit.ts`, pure) then a write naming the digest it was read at; a `CONFLICT` shows the version that is there (Reload or Keep my edits). The app never lints or validates a plan itself.
- A run's agent starts only from a person's act: **Open a session** (`POST /runs/:run/start`, the conductor) or **Drive in background** (`POST /runs/:run/drive`), offered only where nothing works on the run (`idleRuns`). Coming to a screen starts no process: the Terminal tab shows a run's terminal once its session lives or the person pressed "Open a session".
- A screen says an empty list only when the daemon answered one: data not read yet or a read that failed is never "Nothing open" (`readingOf`, `src/shared/model/freshness.ts`); a failed read and stale data (the reads after a good one fail) are one line, `<Freshness>` (`src/shared/components/freshness.tsx`). Every request has a deadline (`TIMEOUTS` in `api.ts`: 15 s for a GET, 120 s for a change) and an answer that is not the daemon's envelope names its status and path (`readAnswer`), never a JSON parser's message. The daemon's pulse (`/health` every 4 s, `src/shared/daemon/heartbeat.ts`) makes the top bar read **not answering** while the sockets stay open to a stopped or stuck daemon. A run or a chat the route names is "not found" only on the daemon's word read after the screen opened (`useFound`, `found.ts`), never while it may have just been made.
- With no daemon the shell draws one panel (`NoDaemon`) instead of the screens, so no screen shows empty data as if it were true. In the Tauri window the app starts the daemon itself (ADR-0101): `autostart` in `model.ts` decides when, `src/shared/daemon/shell.ts` asks the shell's `open_repo` for the repository's daemon (`metator serve --ensure` with the bundled CLI, ADR-0105). Repositories are added from the app (round 20, ADR-0105): the shell's commands are one typed wrapper, `src/shared/platform/tauri-commands.ts` (`invoke` and `listen`; a refusal is `{ code, message, hint }`), with a fake of the same interface, `src/shared/platform/fake-commands.ts`, that the unit tests use and the e2e puts in through `window.__METATOR_FAKE__`; in a browser there are none (`appCommands` is undefined) and Add repository lists the commands to run (`webCommands`). What an inspection means and the next action are `readInspection` (from the CLI's `next`, never re-derived), the steps of Add repository are one transition function, `flowStep` (pick → inspect → host → Set up with its output as one line, `progressLine` → the commit card, Commit or Not now → Open), the switcher's rows are `switcherRows`, and what the main area shows instead of the daemon's screens is `shellView` (first run only in the app's shell with no repository known); all pure in `src/features/repos/repos.ts`. A commit is only ever the person's click, of the files setup wrote; a repository already known is opened, never set up again; "Remove from the app" forgets it and deletes nothing. The daemon is started through `open_repo` (`src/shared/daemon/shell.ts`). Dev Containers (round 21, ADR-0106) are pure in `src/features/repos/devcontainers.ts`: the engine's list in words (`readContainerList`: no engine names Docker Desktop and Rancher Desktop, no dev container says "open it once in VS Code, or run devcontainer up"), its rows (`containerRows`: Start for a stopped one, Choose, Open for one the app knows), the steps before the round-20 flow (`containerStep`: list → Start → pick → install with its lines), then the same `flowStep` runs with every command bound to the container (`inContainer`) and reads "in the container" (`readInspection`'s `where`), its host check always shown with the engine's `fix` (a `devcontainer.json` feature line or a command). A dev container's entry is `kind: "devcontainer"`, keyed by the shell (`devcontainer:` + its local folder label), named `shop (Dev Container)` (`repoName`) with its container's state (`containerStateOf`); a stopped or unreachable one shows `ContainerDown` (Start, Reconnect; `containerDown`, `shellView`'s `container-down`). Its editor is never the daemon's: `editorChoice` builds the engine's vscode-remote link and the shell opens it on this computer (`useHostEditor`, through `runControls`). The Tauri shell (`src-tauri/src`, ADR-0105) holds no domain logic: its commands (`lib.rs`) run the `metator` it resolves (`cli.rs`: the bundled sidecar first, `$METATOR_BIN`, or the person's choice in Settings) with the composed `PATH` and `METATOR_RESOURCES` (`runner.rs`, `paths.rs`), read the CLI's envelope (`envelope.rs`), keep `repos.json` and `settings.json` as versioned documents (`store.rs`), write the `metator` launcher only on a click (`launcher.rs`) and find the Linux CLI bundle (`bundle.rs`). For a dev container (ADR-0106) they run the app's `metator devcontainer …` (`devcontainer.rs`: the command lines, the key `devcontainer:<local folder>`, VS Code links only for `open_uri`), a reason in the CLI's error (`details.reason`) becomes the refusal's code (`CONTAINER_STOPPED`, `MUSL`…, `envelope.rs`), and `open_repo` joins the window to the daemon in the container through a loopback forwarder (`forward.rs`: one `docker exec -i … metator tunnel` per connection, the port kept per repository, re-pointed on Reconnect). The decisions are pure functions tested with `cargo test`; `runner.rs` has an ignored test over the real compiled CLI (`METATOR_TEST_APP_DIR`). The sidecar and resources come in only through `tauri.bundle.conf.json` and `tauri.linux-cli.conf.json` (`--config` in `desktop.yml`), so `cargo test` and `tauri dev` need no compiled CLI.
- One confirm: what cannot be taken back asks first through `src/shared/confirm.ts` (`confirmed`; Done and Drop of a task, which the daemon cannot reopen), and closing a live pane or a chat whose agent runs asks through `useConfirmClose` while `ui.confirmClosePane` is on: on Terminals, on a run's Terminal tab and on **Close chat** alike.
- A refusal the app can offer a way past is recognized by `error.details` (`refusedForDirtyTree`), never by the message; the way past is a button in the same `Notice`.
- A system plan's step is numbered by its place in the plan's deploy order (`stepPlace`), the same in the sidebar (`stepOf`) and on a card (`groupStepText`); the count of children started so far is never the total. A system run's plan is the one the daemon names for it (`RunOverview.systemPlan`, the plan's id) before any match by task (`systemPlanOf`, `systemRunOf`): the planner words the plan's task its own way. Its plan-approval card shows that plan in full: the flow, then the steps per repository unfolded (`SystemPlanFull`).
- A question read from a terminal (`isTerminalQuestion`: an agent's question with `Attach and answer in the pane`) is answered on the card; Attach goes through `answerIn` to the run's Terminal tab, which attaches, focuses the pane and scrolls to its question. A row is a terminal ask that opens the pane only when its key is `terminal:` (`isTerminalAsk`).
- An option the app cannot send is closed with its reason (`optionClosed`: the daemon's `disabled`/`disabledBecause`, or Approve on a plan whose lint has errors), never hidden; on a plan's card a lint error offers **Ask the planner to fix it** instead.
- The app sends no request it knows will fail: an option the daemon does not list (`system.roots` on an older daemon) has no control, and `/scratch` is asked only when the state counts debug changes. The conversation agent's first stage is pure in `stage1.ts`: Open diff that is no answer (`opensDiff`), a commit or push that needs consent (`consentOf`), what removing debug changes did (`dropText`).
- Work is shown as parent tasks (`tasks.ts`, from the Board's cards): the sidebar's rows and the Board's top level; a task's board and sidebar tree list its steps and child runs by repository. A system task's flow is drawn only on its page. A run's board column is the daemon's `phase` (core `workPhase`), never guessed from stage names (`board.ts`); a system plan's flow is `plan-flow.ts` (pure), drawn by `PlanFlowGraph`.
- An escalated run is not finished (`isFinished` in `src/shared/model/runs.ts`): it stays in the sidebar (blocked) and is a card on Home (`EscalatedCard`), with Resume and Close run; its page shows the same two actions under the head, on every tab. A `planned` run (`--until plan`, round 17) is finished and reads `plan ready` (`runStateOf`; `done` on the first level). With no decision waiting, Home says "nothing" only when nothing stands still either (`quietHeading`, `quietInboxText`); a blocked task says what it needs (`taskNeed`).
- Agent text is never HTML: an artifact or an item's analysis is blocks of text, headings and code (`artifactBlocks`, `MarkdownBlocks`). The Backlog's analysis and plan (round 17, ADR-0096) are pure in `src/features/backlog/model.ts`: the freshness badge (`freshnessText`, `freshnessTone`), which of Analyse / Make plan / Implement an item offers and why one is closed (`itemButtons`: Make plan closed while the analysis is stale, Implement while `waitsFor` is not empty, "Review plan, then implement" for a stale plan, neither on a parent with children), a row's one word (`itemWord`), a parent's parts (`childRows`, `childrenProgress`, the daemon's `progress` first), each child under its parent (`backlogRows`); freshness and what an item waits for are the daemon's (`GET /issues`), never computed here. A button that starts an agent shows its terminal at once (`shownRoute`), as "+ New chat" opens its thread. A system plan step's tile (flow or Board card) opens `StepDetailDialog` (`stepDetail`; its Backlog part is `itemOfStep`); "Create Backlog item" on a plan view is `FromPlanButton` ("Open its Backlog item" once `itemOfPlan` finds the parent); `#/backlog/<id>` chooses an item. Reviews (round 18, ADR-0097) are pure in `src/features/reviews/model.ts`: a watched MR's and my MR's one word (`watchedWord`, `mineWord`), a finding's badge (`findingBadge`, looks in `LOOKS.finding`), when all is fixed (`allFixed`), Home's cards (`reviewCards`: asked to review → Review, new commits or replies → Re-review, all fixed → approve Yes/No, a new review on my MR → Analyse; none while an agent works on the MR) as rows of `needsQueue`'s queue (`reviewNeeds`, kind `review`), and what "Send selected" sends (`sendSelection`: the checked replies by id, `only`); what is new and each finding's state are the daemon's (`GET /reviews`, `GET /mrs`, read by `useReviewLists`). A publish is the run's approval gate, on the decision card.

## Allowed dependencies

React, Vite, xterm.js and the Tauri API (ADR-0078). From MetatorAI only the types of `@metator/core` (`import type`, a dev dependency, ADR-0085): the e2e test (`e2e/desktop.e2e.test.ts`) is where the client and the daemon meet at run time.

## Pitfalls

- The daemon answers with permissive CORS because the app is another origin; the daemon stays on localhost.
- `react` and `react-dom` are pinned to one exact version: a mismatch is React error #527 at start, with a blank window.
- Building the Tauri package needs Rust and the platform's webview; the web bundle alone (`bun run build`) is what CI tests. A focused xterm stops the propagation of the keys it handles: a window-level key listener (the prefix, Escape for a menu) must register in the capture phase (S6).
- A `<dialog>` opened with `showModal()` makes the page behind it inert: a window-level key listener must give way while `dialog[open]` exists, or a key meant for the dialog also runs a shortcut.
- The e2e tests find parts of the screens by class (`.needs .item`, `.backlog .notice`, `.review .line.add`, `.session .head`): renaming a class is a change of the tests too.
